sources.title: Pre-Suasion | Simon & Schuster
sources.role: primary authorized metadata, official excerpt, edition confirmation, and narrow chapter-7-through-chapter-12 concept support
sources.notes: Confirms the Simon & Schuster September 2016 English-language edition, exposes the opening excerpt for Chapter 1, provides official overview framing for the book's pre-suasion concept, and provides narrow official support for Chapter 7 on associations, Chapter 8 on persuasive placement contexts, Chapter 9 on the readied-firing mechanism of pre-suasion, Chapter 10 on the six classic influence-principle roads to change, Chapter 11 on unity as a seventh principle rooted in We identity, family, and place, and Chapter 12 on unity through synchronous or collaborative action.

sources.title: Pre-Suasion: A Revolutionary Way to Influence and Persuade | Google Play Books
sources.role: supporting bibliographic metadata and distributor confirmation
sources.notes: Confirms the ebook is sold by Simon & Schuster and reports 432 pages in the same 2016 text family.

sources.title: Pre-Suasion A Revolutionary Way to Influence and Persuade | Thalia
sources.notes: Captures the full 14-chapter contents listing plus parts. Used narrowly for chapter titles and ordering because the official Simon & Schuster page exposes only a partial TOC in the fetched HTML.

sources.title: Pre-suasion : a revolutionary way to influence and persuade | Penn Libraries
sources.role: dust-jacket style chapter-map and privileged-moments overview support
sources.notes: Confirms the full contents line and summarizes the book's claim about privileged moments for change, receptivity before the message, and redirected focus of attention.

sources.title: Pre-Suasion | Admired Leadership
sources.role: chapter 2 concept support for privileged moments and self-relevant opener examples
sources.notes: Provides narrow summary support for privileged moments, attention at the moment of decision, and the helpful-person / adventurous-person question examples used to frame Chapter 2.

sources.title: Pre-suasion - Robert Cialdini | chidwi
sources.role: chapter 3 and chapter 4 concept support for attention-importance and focal-causal framing
sources.notes: Provides narrow summary support that attention elevates importance, that what is focal can be treated as causal, and that helping-norm style framing belongs to the early part of the book. Used only as secondary support when the authorized preview is thin.

sources.title: Pre-Suasion, by Robert Cialdini | Well That Makes Sense
sources.role: chapter 5 concept support for attractors, especially survival-linked and goal-fitting attention triggers
sources.notes: Provides narrow summary support that some cues attract attention with unusual force, including threatening, different, and goal-fitting stimuli. Used only to support chapter-local framing for the attractors chapter.

sources.title: Pre-suasion by Robert Cialdini | ICPL catalog record snippet
sources.role: chapter 6 concept support for magnetizers that keep attention engaged
sources.notes: Provides narrow summary support that some information has intrinsic pull and staying power, including self-relevant, unfinished, and mysterious cues. Used only to support chapter-local framing for the magnetizers chapter.
